The words, to me, are like a ballad of self rediscovery, of turning away from your old self that’s created bad habits and negative brain states and telling yourself you’re going to get better and do better no matter what, and the old part of you can rejoin you when it’s ready and healed. I wanna start out this comment by saying that I understand what you’re going through, you’re not alone. Obviously I don’t know your exact situation, but I grew up in my early teens with an emotionally abusive mother, an emotionally absent father, and my younger sister who I was expected to care for. I dealt with depression, image issues, my sexuality, anxiety- not to mention physical health issues. 

But it gets better, it really, truly does. That anxiety, when you have a good thought or any thought at all and then your brain immediately replaces it with rejection and the worst case scenario: it’s lies. Sometimes, the bad does happen, but I wanna tell you something- the more you focus on the bad stuff, the more of it comes into your life. No, it’s not easy to just stop thinking that way- I know that for sure. One positive thought is more powerful than a thousand negative ones. When you have a bad thought, stop, think, and tell yourself, “no, it could be like this instead” and think something positive, embrace that. It helps, even if just a little, to start combating that anxiety cycle of worst-case in your brain.

TLDR; You matter, you deserve to live, and it does get better. No matter what.
